name: Sheh-Ara
held_by: Nobody; scavengers and wildlife
summary: Sheh-Ara is a half-sunken stilt village south of Lujei, emptied by raiders from the Rose and left to the lake.

name: Oru-Neel
held_by: Nobody; scavengers and wildlife
summary: Oru-Neel is a stilt village in the north-east farm country, emptied when its dyke failed and salt water came into the rice paddies.

name: Meris-Keth
held_by: No one
summary: Meris-Keth is an abandoned stilt village in the south-east Banujha Basin, left when its Hist sickened and its families carried their eggs to Jarecai's tree. Khajiit smugglers now use its halls, and its unstaked dead walk.

name: Zeh-Orun
held_by: Nobody; scavengers
summary: A stilt village on the cape abandoned after the 3E 427 uprisings.

name: Zul-Etha
held_by: Nobody; scavengers and wildlife
summary: Zul-Etha is a drowned village in the southern washes, a carting stage emptied when the Soulrest gold trade ended in 3E 427.

name: Acra-Tiin
held_by: Soulrest merchant council through a village reeve
summary: Acra-Tiin is a fishing village on the south shore of the cape, across the water from Soulrest's southern islands. It sends fish and salt to the port.

name: Agia Nero
held_by: Wild; scavengers
summary: A ruined Imperial post west of Loriasel on the high ground, its walls broken and its yard sunk.

name: Amalaja
held_by: The village elders, paying the island core little for protection
summary: Amalaja is a seaward village at the east end of the washes, close to the delta, where Blackrose's channels meet the Lilmoth coast. It trades fish for the delta's rice.

name: Aphon Belvedere
held_by: A small Archwardens' customs watch of Archein-descended families
summary: Aphon Belvedere is a lookout house on Aphon Isle, an old Imperial retreat now used by the Archwardens as a customs watch over Topal Bay.

name: Archon
held_by: A harbour authority and merchant council in the East Empire Company's old buildings, with the successor state's customs officers alongside
summary: Archon is the province's best working harbour and its principal legal port, on the Padomaic coast where an estuary meets the sea. Amphibious civic life is ordinary here: children play underwater, guar breathe water, cargo moves above and below the surface. A sealed Shadowscale school stands closed in the town.

name: Armanias
held_by: A Lukiul village of potters and rice-growers under Gideon's council
summary: Armanias is a village on the coast road south of Gideon, known for red-clay pottery fired in kilns on the dry ground. It sells to Gideon and to Soulrest-bound caravans.

name: Arorha
held_by: Arorha village elders, answering to the Aroxhu council
summary: Arorha is a clay-mound village on the southern shore of Hatandros Bight, the confederacy's sea door. Its people ship Okuwun-Rahei clay and dye north to Thorn and south to Archon, and take tolls from boats that land.

name: Aroxhu
held_by: The council of village elders of the Oxhu-Teeleel, meeting under the Aroxhu Hist
summary: Aroxhu is the great mound-town of the Clay-Mound People, the largest tribal settlement of the east interior. Its council of elders speaks for the whole confederacy and meets under its Hist.

name: Ayiin
held_by: The Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac
summary: Ayiin is a hamlet of stone and timber on a river on the east side of the mesa, a day south of Thorn. Its families quarry and watch the road to Balormaak.

name: Orimel
held_by: Wild; the Veesa-Teeleel keep watch from afar
summary: A small Barsaebic Ayleid ruin on the high ground north-west of Slough Point, with white arches in the reeds and a flooded undercroft.

name: Anutasil
held_by: Wild
summary: A small Barsaebic ayleid ruin in the western marsh, white arches in the reeds.

name: Mirasel
held_by: Wild; the Veesa-Teeleel keep watch from afar
summary: A small Barsaebic ayleid ruin on a sedge island east of Loriasel, with white arches in the reeds and a flooded undercroft.

name: Badal
held_by: A council of village elders answering to the mound confederacy of Aroxhu
summary: Badal is a clay-mound village on the shore of an inlet at the north of the bayou, on the road to the mound country. Its potters and dyers send pots and pigment down the rivers to Archon.

name: Bala Karag
held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts and sea-birds
summary: Bala Karag is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi stronghold on a small rocky island a day's walk from Thorn. The Knahaten Flu emptied it and its lower halls are flooded.

name: Balormaak
held_by: Nothing living; the flu-dead and what they guard
summary: Balormaak is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi town on the eastern mesa, south of Ayiin. The Knahaten Flu emptied it and jungle has grown over it since.

name: Bell Station
held_by: A salvage-and-watch crew sent out by Lilmoth's merchant council to dive the drowned spires, who owe it a share of each haul in kind
summary: Bell Station is a timber platform anchored over the drowned spires of Benthic Yobesh, from which divers are lowered in brass bells. It is held by a small crew of Lilmoth's delta families, who dive the spires and watch the deep for the merchant council and pay it a share of what they raise.

name: Blackrose
held_by: The island core: a narrow, defensive, self-perpetuating government whose legitimacy is possession
summary: Blackrose is a lake-island city where three rivers meet, ringed by stilt districts and boardwalks over the water. It is the hinge of the south, tolling everything that moves between Murkwood, Oliis Bay, eastern Blackwood and Bramman's river. Its people are the oddest mix in the province and trust no institution.

name: Blackrose Prison
held_by: The Blackguards' heirs under a Naga raj-kaal; the risen inmates in the lower levels
summary: The Rose is the Second Empire's fortress prison, built in a day from the ruins of Lilmothiit Blackrose. In 4E 201 it is held by the prison-born Blackguards' heirs under a Naga raj-kaal, and its drowned lower levels hold the risen dead of its old inmates.

name: Bucalos
held_by: Nobody; scavengers and wildlife
summary: Bucalos is a Kothringi-named stilt town beside Toklea, abandoned when its people moved into the larger town.

name: Sahlpesh Cave
held_by: A Sarpa warband
summary: Sahlpesh Cave is a cave in the mesa's foot beside the Sarpa camp, used by the Sarpa as a roost and larder. It lies on the edge of the Middle Argonian interior.

name: Kelp-Mouth Cave
held_by: Smugglers of Topal Bay, using it as a cache
summary: Kelp-Mouth Cave is a sea cave on Aphon Isle's eastern shore, where a Khajiit smuggling crew keeps moon sugar out of sight of the Warden watch at the Belvedere.

name: Chasepoint
held_by: Soulrest merchant council through a village reeve
summary: Chasepoint is the coast road stage east of Soulrest, a wreck-salvage and carting village on the Percar road. It stands where the road meets the first fork of the interior river.

name: Delta Ferry
held_by: Delta ferry-folk, kin to the Lilmoth boatmen, who keep the crossing with the merchant council's goodwill
summary: Delta Ferry is the crossing east of Blackrose where the road to Lilmoth meets the water. Rafts carry freight, rice and travellers across the delta channel.

name: Echo Deep
held_by: Dreugh and the deep
summary: Echo Deep is a trench in the sea floor east of Lilmoth where sounds return from the dark. Divers who go down to it report voices in the water. Dreugh hunt along its edge.

name: Dunhallow Plantation
held_by: A Lilmoth family that took over the empty planter house, worked by tenant kin
summary: Dunhallow is a rice estate north-west of Lilmoth, set in the shell of a Breton planter's house that stood empty from the Third Era. A Lilmoth family took it over in the generations after 4E 48, and tenant kin work its paddies.

name: Silt-Orrel Estate
held_by: An Argonian family of Lilmoth that settled the empty planter house, worked by tenant kin
summary: Silt-Orrel is a small rice and reed estate on the road north of Lilmoth, set in the shell of an Archein planter's house. An Argonian family took the empty house after 4E 48 and hires out its boats to Lilmoth's harbour.

name: Mereweather Estate
held_by: An Argonian family that settled the empty planter house, with tenant kin
summary: Mereweather is a coastal rice estate on the south shore of the northern island, near Fort Reedmoth, in the shell of an Archein planter's house. An Argonian family settled it after 4E 48 and sends its rice by lighter to Archon or Lilmoth.

name: Ixa-Ruu Farm
held_by: A single farm family in the Lilmoth coast's orbit
summary: A small coastal farm at the south end of the southern island, near Southwatch Keep, growing roots and keeping fowl.

name: Seeku Farm
held_by: A single farm family in the Lilmoth coast's orbit
summary: A farm west of Lilmoth on firm ground, growing reed-roots and keeping marsh-guar.

name: Wattle-Pool Farm
held_by: A single farm family in the Lilmoth coast's orbit
summary: A farm on the island's firm centre, with fruit trees and a pool teeming with fish.

name: Tal-Neesh Farm
held_by: A single farm family in the Lilmoth coast's orbit
summary: A farm between Sal-Axan and Fort Reedmoth on the island road, growing rice for the fort's keepers.

name: Brineflat Farm
held_by: A Seafalls family
summary: Brineflat Farm is a salt-and-sedge farm on the flats behind Seafalls, kept by one Spray-Folk family.

name: Saltmeadow Farm
held_by: A Seafalls family
summary: Saltmeadow Farm is a grazing and rice farm south of Brineflat, kept by a Spray-Folk household that herds guar.

name: Reedfall Farm
held_by: A rice-farming family
summary: A rice farm in the farmed land east of Blackrose, on the road to Tei-Kur. It sells to Tei-Kur and Delta Ferry.

name: Vandrel Farm
held_by: The Vandrel family, tenants of Stormhold's farm-holders
summary: A raised stone farmstead of one Dunmer-descended family, south-west of Fort Willowmoth, growing saltrice for Stormhold.

name: Urvyn Farm
held_by: The Urvyn family
summary: A raised stone farmstead west of Jal-Veesa on the northern road.

name: Fort Chalkmoth
held_by: The Archwardens' garrison, ex-Archein families
summary: Fort Chalkmoth is a stone fort on the mesa top above Noota Nara, held by a small garrison of the Archwardens. It guards the chalk pit and the road across the mesa.

name: Fort Gysilla
held_by: An Archwardens garrison of old Archein families
summary: Fort Gysilla is an old Imperial stone fort on a lake island at the south of Lake Ulaish, now an Archwardens toll and watch station. Its small garrison collects the toll on boat traffic between Truowa and the southern waters and watches the lake.

name: Fort Reedmoth
held_by: A small garrison of the Archwardens, the An-Xileel successor administration, drawn from old Archein families
summary: Fort Reedmoth is a stone fort at the east end of the northern Althii island, held by a small Archwarden garrison as a toll station on the island road and the boat crossing to Archon's coast.

name: Fort Rustmoth
held_by: An Archwarden customs garrison keeping the old Imperial fort
summary: A stone Imperial keep beside Slough Point, held as the western customs fort on the Blackwood Road. The Imperial eagle still hangs over the gate. It has not been chiselled off.

name: Fort Shellmoth
held_by: A small garrison of the Archwardens, Archein-descended
summary: Fort Shellmoth is an Imperial-built coastal fort near Soulrest, held by the Archwardens as a harbour watch and customs station.

name: Fort Silvermoth
held_by: An Archwarden toll garrison drawn from old Archein families
summary: Fort Silvermoth is an Imperial-built stone fort on the coast road between Gideon and Soulrest, now held by the Archwardens as a toll station. Its garrison keeps Imperial manners and Argonian oaths.

name: Fort Swiftmoth
held_by: No one holds it; Aroxhu families shelter in its upper floor and smugglers cache goods in its cellars
summary: Fort Swiftmoth is a stone keep on firm ground inland from Archon, empty since the Legion left at the secession and never re-garrisoned by the Archwardens. Smugglers keep goods in its cellars, and Aroxhu families rest in its dry upper floor.

name: Fort Thornmoth
held_by: The Archwardens' garrison, staffed by ex-Archein families
summary: Fort Thornmoth is a stone fort a short way west of Thorn, built by the Empire and held in 4E 201 by a small garrison of the Archwardens. It is the toll gate on the road into Thorn and a watch over the bay.

name: Fort Willowmoth
held_by: The Archwardens' frontier screen (an Argonian garrison keeping the old Imperial fort)
summary: A stone Imperial fort a short walk east of Stormhold, held by an Archwarden garrison as a toll station and river watch on the Morrowind border road. The eagle still hangs over the gate.

name: Gandranen
held_by: Wild; the Fenlord's undead guards and the library's own magic
summary: A Barsaebic Ayleid ruin in the fetid mires, with a book-drawing magical library, built by a sorceress of Hermaeus Mora and the tomb of a Fenlord.

name: Gaweja
held_by: Gaweja elders, under the Aroxhu council
summary: Gaweja is a lakeside clay-mound village on the road between Yulca and Badal. It fishes, grows rice on its mound slopes and trades fish to the Agaceph.

name: Gemin
held_by: Wild; haunted; no one holds it
summary: The partially flooded, monster-infested ruin of the Conclave of Baal's vaults, north-west of Stormhold, where the tablet that finds Murkwood was kept.

name: Gideon
held_by: The Gideon civic council in the old Governor's Mansion, over a Lukiul Argonian majority with Nibenese-descended families
summary: Gideon is the western frontier city of Black Marsh, built on the dry road through a flooded hillscape and on the Ayleid ruins of Twyllbek. In 4E 201 it keeps a courthouse and a civic council in the old Governor's Mansion, and it openly denies the Archwardens' claim to rule it.

name: Giovesse
held_by: Gideon's poorer families and ghost-hunters, who squat below the ruined Castle Giovesse
summary: Giovesse is a hamlet of squatters' huts at the foot of haunted Castle Giovesse, within arm's reach of Gideon's north gate. People live here for the cheap ground and the chance of finding what the Empire left.

name: Gul-Tej
held_by: A council of Lukiul and Naka-Desh trader families
summary: Gul-Tej is a market town on the eastern road out of Gideon, where Naka-Desh river stations, Archein landholders and caravan drivers trade. It stands on a river fork and sits at the edge of the interior.

name: Guxal
held_by: The Root-Folk of Helstrom, a sap-gathering clan
summary: Guxal is a hamlet of stilt houses on the south shore of the bay, a hunting and sap-gathering station of Root-Folk families. They trade fish and sap to Thorn but have no other dealings with the city.

name: Helstrom
held_by: The Helstrom assembly of interior naheesh and tree-minders; a tribal levy keeps the guard
summary: Helstrom is the interior capital of Black Marsh, a great city that no invader has taken, on the river fork at the heart of the Hist forest. In 4E 201 a standing assembly of tribal elders and tree-minders runs it. It hosts the great Root Talk each Hist-Tsoko. Outsiders may enter on sufferance. The city's real danger is its own guard and alleys.

name: Hirecan
held_by: The Agaceph
summary: Hirecan is a small hamlet of the needle-faced Agaceph, on a river in the south of the mesa. They are travellers and readers, wary of strangers.

name: Hixinoag
held_by: A drifting community of Lukiul and Naka-Desh families under a headwoman
summary: Hixinoag is a raft village on the northern caravan road above Gideon: house-rafts moored to stakes in a ring of channels, joined to the road by a plank causeway. It is Gideon's northern waystation and the first stop for caravans from the lake country.

name: Tidewatch Homestead
held_by: A lone Spray-Folk household
summary: Tidewatch Homestead is a lone house on the shore south of Brineflat. Its household twists nets and rope for Seafalls and watches the beach for smugglers.

name: Icalca
held_by: The Agaceph of Icalca, a raft-folk
summary: Icalca is a hamlet of Agaceph raft-folk on the western lake. They are illusionists who sell tomes and spells, and who freeze intruders before they decide what to do with them.

name: Fort Sallowmoth
held_by: Unheld; smugglers, snakes and the odd squatter
summary: A ruined Imperial fort on the road between Karketa and Lilmoth, empty since the Legion left at the secession.

name: Brackwater Waystation
held_by: Abandoned to smugglers, snakes and the odd squatter
summary: A ruined Imperial waystation on the south shore east of Lilmoth, once a customs shed and signal tower.

name: Mudmoth
held_by: Nobody; a few outlaws shelter in its cellars
summary: Mudmoth is a ruined Imperial road station in the southern washes, left at the secession. Mir-Xal took over the road's toll, so the Archwardens never re-held it.

name: Fort Lowmoth
held_by: Road bandits, with snakes and the odd squatter
summary: A burnt Imperial fort on the island road near Fort Reedmoth, left as a ruin because Reedmoth's garrison is too small to hold both.

name: Mistwatch
held_by: Nobody; scavengers
summary: Mistwatch is a ruined Imperial signal tower on the cape's south shore, left at the secession and used by smugglers.

name: Aldanus Watchtower
held_by: Wild
summary: A ruined Imperial watchtower on the border hills in the far west.

name: Nine Reeds Waystation
held_by: No one: bandits and smugglers shelter in it
summary: Nine Reeds Waystation is an Imperial ruin in the Nha Enasa, a stone tower with a granary and a signal fire on the road north of Gideon.

name: Wrackmoth
held_by: Nobody; scavengers
summary: Wrackmoth is a ruined Imperial fort on the cape's north coast, left at the secession and never re-held.

name: Gideon South Watch
held_by: No one: bandits and smugglers shelter in it
summary: Gideon South Watch is an Imperial ruin in the Kotherra Mangroves, a watch tower on the south side of Gideon built to watch the delta approaches.

name: Aphon Signal Tower
held_by: No one: bandits and smugglers shelter in it
summary: Aphon Signal Tower is an Imperial ruin on Aphon Isle, a signal tower on the island's high ground paired with Aphon Belvedere to watch the bay.

name: Calvian Waystation
held_by: Wild; scavengers shelter in it
summary: A ruined Imperial road waystation north of Jal-Veesa, roofless and half sunk in mud.

name: Inoio
held_by: A Three Waters raft-master family under the elder of Uluo
summary: Inoio is a Three Waters hamlet where the east road crosses a bayou channel by raft ferry. It is the only crossing for days and tolls nothing, because the elder wants the traffic to talk.

name: Inoja
held_by: Inoja elders, under the Aroxhu council
summary: Inoja is the market town of the clay-mound country, on the river crossing south of Aroxhu. It is the confederacy's main trading post for outsiders.

name: Jal-Veesa
held_by: The Veesa-Teeleel elders; their own, not the Vicecanons
summary: A market town of reed boats, mats and dried fish beside a Hist pool, west of Stormhold on the northern road. The Sedge-Wardens who live here keep the reed beds and fish weirs that feed Stormhold and watch the Ayleid ruins of their country.

name: Jarecai
held_by: The Mine-Burner tribes' council of elders
summary: Jarecai is the seat of the Mine-Burner tribes of the Banujha Basin, a fortified stilt town on the water behind Soulrest. It is the hold over Soulrest's hatching grounds and the heart of the tribes that burned the Imperial mines.

name: Joxhi
held_by: Joxhi elders, under the Aroxhu council
summary: Joxhi is a village of clay-diggers on a river bend north of Inoja. Its pits give the deepest red clay of the Aroxhu country, and the village stands on its own spoil.

name: Julo
held_by: A family of causeway farmers in the Stormhold manner
summary: Julo is a hamlet of stone-footed farmhouses at the mouth of the river braid where it enters the north-west corner of Lake Ulaish. A few families farm saltrice and run a ferry across the braid.

name: Ka-Asei
held_by: The village elders, paying the island core for protection
summary: Ka-Asei is a stilt village over the water at the lake's southeast, a day from Blackrose, sitting where the channel to the delta begins.

name: Kaochalit
held_by: Nothing living; the flu-dead and what they guard
summary: Kaochalit is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi settlement on the mesa top south of Tsonac. The Knahaten Flu killed its people and the Stone-Sleepers avoid its halls.

name: Karketa
held_by: A village moot answering to Lilmoth's council
summary: Karketa is a fishing and ferry village on the western coast of the southern Althii island, a few hours' walk from Lilmoth. It supplies the town with fish and salt and watches the sea road to Southwatch Keep.

name: Kharaxos
held_by: Mine-Burner elders, under Jarecai
summary: Kharaxos is a Mine-Burner town on the east of the Banujha Basin, its name a leftover from the Kothringi who held the shore, which the tribes never changed. It trades with Kothringi-named towns of the interior.

name: Khariton
held_by: Nobody; scavengers and wildlife, and a Blackguard watch post
summary: Khariton is a Kothringi-named town of the resettled interior, abandoned as its channel silted and left to the washes.

name: Kharraluhl
held_by: Nothing living; scavengers and the dead
summary: Kharraluhl is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi settlement on the high ground north of the bay, a short ride from Thorn. The Knahaten Flu killed its people and it has stood empty since.

name: Khiar
held_by: Khiar elders, under the Aroxhu council
summary: Khiar is a fishing village of clay-mound people on the southern cape of Okuwun-Rahei, near the Seafalls coast. Its boats supply fish to the mound country.

name: Kornakim
held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
summary: Kornakim is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi watch-hold on a sandy headland halfway down Hatandros Bight. It was abandoned after the Knahaten Flu and sits above the surf, shunned.

name: Korydon
held_by: A council of craft-guild elders of the Chime-Keepers
summary: Korydon is the principal Chime-Keeper town of the interior, on a ring of dry ground encircled by water between Helstrom and the southern lakes. Argonians resettled it after the Kothringi died out and kept its name. It is orderly, prosperous for the marsh and known for tin-and-copper chimes, metal-woven rope and shallow-draft boats.

name: Kyrenos
held_by: No one: the dead, diggers and Naka-Desh chime-hangers
summary: Kyrenos is a Kothringi ruin in the Banujha Basin: a long music-hall whose columns once held rows of chimes. Mine-Burner watchers guard its last chimes, and its dead walk the colonnade.

name: Meliton
held_by: Wild; the Naka-Desh visit to hang chimes
summary: A dead Kothringi town of cairns and stone footings in the western hills, left empty since the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560.

name: Pelaxis
held_by: No one: the dead, diggers and Naka-Desh chime-hangers
summary: Pelaxis is a Kothringi ruin in the Nha Enasa: a river quay and a boat-house for shallow-draft Kothringi sail-and-paddle boats. Its rotten quay draws timber-scavengers, and its drowned boatwrights keep the boat-house.

name: Dorianth
held_by: No one: the dead, diggers and Naka-Desh chime-hangers
summary: Dorianth is a Kothringi ruin in the Nha Enasa: a hall with a leviathan-horn carved on its lintel, the longhouse of a seafaring family. Hunters shelter in it from the rain, and its strongroom door is still shut.

name: Mnemosa
held_by: No one: the dead, diggers and Naka-Desh chime-hangers
summary: Mnemosa is a Kothringi ruin in the Nha Enasa: a terrace of burial stones with a ring of chime-posts. The Naka-Desh guard its graves from looters, and its dead rise at night.

name: Aithros
held_by: Wild; the Naka-Desh visit to hang chimes
summary: Aithros is a dead Kothringi town of cairns and stone footings above a stream, a day south-west of Hutan-Veel near the Cyrodiil border. The Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 emptied it.

name: Calyphe
held_by: No one: the dead, diggers and Naka-Desh chime-hangers
summary: Calyphe is a Kothringi ruin in the Kotherra Mangroves: a Dibella shrine of leaf-carved stone half sunk in mangrove roots. It is unheld; Gideon's diggers prise out its stone and Naka-Desh hang chimes over the altar.

name: Eurydike
held_by: No one: the dead, diggers and Naka-Desh chime-hangers
summary: Eurydike is a Kothringi ruin in the Kotherra Mangroves: the hall of Kothringi knights who served in Gideon's Second-Era garrison. Its dead still walk the barracks, and Gideon's diggers work its tombs.

name: Mistfall Light
held_by: An Archwarden light-keeper family
summary: Mistfall Light is a lighthouse on the south coast of the Sea of Mists, kept by the Archwardens to warn ships off the shoals.

name: Lilmoth
held_by: A reconstituted merchant council; no ruler
summary: Lilmoth is the Festering Jewel of Black Marsh, destroyed in 4E 48 and rebuilt smaller as a wholly Argonian stilt town over a mass grave. Its Old Imperial quarter lies drowned and unrepaired. A young Hist grows in the lower town. It is feared and tended under a rotating guard of tree-minders.

name: Kit Mounds
held_by: Nobody; wildlife and the occasional scholar
summary: Kit Mounds is a cluster of turf domes near the south: a Lilmothiit den, a fox-folk burrow of turf and leaf left from before the Knahaten Flu.

name: Brushmound
held_by: Nobody; wildlife and the occasional scholar
summary: Brushmound is a bramble-covered den north-east of Ka-Asei: a Lilmothiit den, a fox-folk burrow of turf and leaf left from before the Knahaten Flu.

name: Ashiit Den
held_by: Unheld; the spirits of the dead and what has taken to their den
summary: A ruined Lilmothiit den-village of turf-and-leaf domes on the south-western shore of the southern island, empty since the Knahaten Flu.

name: Kitsa Burrow
held_by: Smugglers in the tunnels, and the spirits of the dead
summary: A small ruined Lilmothiit burrow-village at the southern tip of the island, with tunnels under the dunes that smugglers now use.

name: Reknaa-iit Mound
held_by: Left to the spirits of the dead and what has taken to the mound
summary: A ruined Lilmothiit den-mound in the centre of the southern island, the largest den on the isle, empty since the Flu.

name: Rushiit Den
held_by: Left to marsh predators and the restless dead
summary: A ruined Lilmothiit den on the northern island's heart, now a lair of marsh predators.

name: Tailfall Mound
held_by: Smugglers in the lower rooms, and the spirits of the dead
summary: A ruined Lilmothiit den on the north-eastern shore of the northern island, close to Fort Reedmoth, where smugglers hide.

name: Tailhollow
held_by: Nobody; wildlife and the occasional scholar
summary: Tailhollow is a waterlogged den in the west washes: a Lilmothiit burrow of turf and leaf, left in the fox-folk's long withdrawal and emptied for good by the Knahaten Flu.

name: Ra'tal Den
held_by: No one
summary: Ra'tal Den is a ruined turf-and-leaf dome of the Lilmothiit, the fox-folk who held the southern coast.

name: Cutbank Camp
held_by: Field-owners of Thorn, worked by hired Argonian crews
summary: Cutbank Camp is a timber camp on the steep cut bank of the bay's inner shore, west of Fort Thornmoth. Its crews fell jungle hardwood and raft it to Thorn for the field-holders who pay them.

name: Redtimber Camp
held_by: Soulrest's timber crew, paying the Mine-Burners in kind
summary: Redtimber Camp is a small timber camp at the basin's south edge, worked for Soulrest's merchant council. It cuts red mangrove and sends logs down the channel.

name: Redgum Camp
held_by: A timber crew of Soulrest-quarter kin, cutting for the merchant council
summary: Redgum Camp is a timber camp in the Percar hills west of Chasepoint. It cuts the red gum and sends logs to Soulrest.

name: Loriasel
held_by: Wild; lamias and keystone-haunted undead
summary: A Barsaebic Ayleid citadel and amphitheatre on a hill over the Venomous Fens, its keystones and its lamia-infested caverns beneath.

name: Lujei
held_by: The village elders, paying the island core for protection
summary: Lujei is a shore village on the west side of the Blackrose lake channels, where the road from the Soulrest side meets the ferry. It tolls the crossing for the island core.

name: Lujei Ferry
held_by: Lujei village ferry crew
summary: A ferry landing with a cable raft across the Blackrose channel west of Lujei. It carries road traffic between the Soulrest side and the island.

name: Luntoc
held_by: A fishing family and its kin
summary: Luntoc is a hamlet on a low island in the south-west of Lake Ulaish. It is the last dry ground between the lake's western shore and its deep water, and the family there fishes, sets eel traps and guides boats through the shoals.

name: Marzai
held_by: The elders of the Clay-Mound People
summary: Marzai is a clay-mound village on the north-east shore of Lake Ulaish, the western outlier of the Aroxhu mound country. A few households fish the lake, fire pottery and ferry goods toward Aroxhu and Truowa.

name: Xanuc Diggings
held_by: The Stone-Sleepers of Oxayo
summary: Xanuc Diggings is a stone quarry and mine in the mesa wall near Oxayo, worked by Stone-Sleepers. Its galleries run under the mesa top, and the north gallery has broken into an older tunnel.

name: Chalkmoth Pit
held_by: The families of Noota Nara, under Fort Chalkmoth's toll
summary: Chalkmoth Pit is the chalk and limestone working that Fort Chalkmoth was built to guard. Noota Nara's families burn its stone to lime for Thorn's mortar and the saltrice pans.

name: Kalaxo Cut
held_by: The Stone-Sleepers of Ayiin
summary: Kalaxo Cut is a stone quarry cut into the mesa's east flank above Ayiin. Its blocks go by cart to Thorn's builders.

name: Coldbrine Mine
held_by: Thorn's field-owners, with a toll to Fort Thornmoth
summary: Coldbrine Mine is a rock-salt working in a low bluff south-west of Thorn, worked for Thorn's field-owners under the toll of Fort Thornmoth. Its salt cures the saltrice and fish that Thorn exports.

name: Tenmal Pits
held_by: A pit-boss and a handful of delvers, by the Vicecanons' leave
summary: A crystal pit in the hills above Tenmal, worked for Stormhold Crystals by a few households.

name: Old Goldseam
held_by: Nobody; scavengers
summary: A derelict gold mine of the Imperial concession, burned out by the tribes in 3E 427.

name: Blackdrift
held_by: Nobody; scavengers
summary: A burned timber-and-gold mine in the Percar hills.

name: Ninth Shaft
held_by: Nobody; scavengers
summary: A numbered Imperial mine on the south side of the cape.

name: Ashfall Cut
held_by: Nobody; scavengers
summary: A burn-scarred open cut near Naxan.

name: Mir-Xal
held_by: A reeve of the Soulrest merchant council
summary: Mir-Xal is the interior stage on the Soulrest-Blackrose road, a market town on a ridge of dry ground in the washes. It collects toll for Soulrest and ships timber and stone to the coast.

name: Myroleon
held_by: A family of chime-keepers
summary: Myroleon is a hamlet at the southern edge of the Ultherus swamp, where the land breaks into channels toward Blackrose. A few families harvest herbs and keep a chime-post that they sound to guide boats through the maze of water.

name: Nacydes
held_by: A family of Chime-Keepers
summary: Nacydes is a hamlet on high ground on the west side of the Aunike Ridge country, the last Chime-Keeper settlement before Paatru and Naga territory. The families keep penned marsh-lizards and trade metal chimes for hides.

name: Natai
held_by: Village elders; the island core's protection is nominal
summary: Natai is a small village at the southern margin of the washes facing the sea, living on shellfish and salt. Its villagers work the shipwreck beyond its shore.

name: Naxan
held_by: Soulrest merchant council through a village reeve
summary: Naxan is a small fishing and timber village on the cape's north coast, the western end of the Topal Bay road.

name: Nemeon
held_by: Chime-Keeper households
summary: Nemeon is a hamlet on a small waterway between the lake and Korydon, a staging stop for boats and herb-gatherers. It is quiet and poor. It keeps an old Kothringi name.

name: Nenria
held_by: Wild; the Veesa-Teeleel watch it from a distance
summary: A small Barsaebic ayleid ruin on a mound in the marsh south of Jal-Veesa, with broken arches and a flooded undercroft.

name: Noota Nara
held_by: A council of village elders; the Clay-Mound families
summary: Noota Nara is a village below Fort Chalkmoth where, in legend, the villagers once heated spear-tips in a dragon's own fire and killed it. Its walls have been rebuilt. The villagers still resent the loss of the dragon's head.

name: Nundi
held_by: A village moot of Lilmoth-coast families
summary: Nundi is a rice and fish village on the south coast of the northern Althii island, on the road between Uluo and the east. It is where the Lilmoth delta's farms meet the Three Waters tribe's trade.

name: Oeneas
held_by: Chime-Keepers, Argonian resettlers of the Kothringi towns
summary: Oeneas is a hamlet of the Chime-Keepers on the water of the basin's eastern reaches. Its tin chimes carry across the water at dusk.

name: Oju
held_by: A village moot of Lilmoth-coast Argonian families, who answer to no one but pay Lilmoth's council a landing toll
summary: Oju is a stilt village on the strait between Archon's coast and the Althii islands. It is a landing and ferry stop for cargo moving between Archon and Lilmoth.

name: Olvani
held_by: A fishing community of Lukiul families, answering to Gideon's harbour officer
summary: Olvani is a coastal fishing village on the estuary west of Gideon, with a ferry landing for the sea road to Aphon Isle. It lives off eels, mullet and fares from the ferry to Aphon Isle.

name: Hollow Tide Camp
held_by: Skeith smugglers, a hardened crew
summary: Hollow Tide Camp is the smugglers' beach camp on the south-west of Skeith Isle. It runs untaxed goods between the isle and the Okuwun-Rahei shore, dodging Archon and Thorn customs.

name: Marque Landing
held_by: Skeith pirates, half-chartered ex-privateers
summary: Marque Landing is the pirates' camp on stilts in the shallows below Rainbreaker Keep. Its crews sail on a half-recognised commission from the Archon coast's privateering tradition.

name: Sedgeweir
held_by: Veesa-Teeleel weir-wardens
summary: A weir-wardens' camp on the river south-east of Stormhold, keeping fish traps and sedge beds that feed the city.

name: Tseli-Oon
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Tseli-Oon is a small outpost on a bank of the river arm that runs north-east out of Helstrom, kept for sap-gathering. Boatmen going up the arm toward the forest tie up here for a night. Few outsiders do.

name: Gaxu-Reet
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Gaxu-Reet is a small outpost where the river arms south-east of Helstrom join and spread into the lake delta, kept for egg-tending and river watch. Boats from Helstrom to the lake's south shore pass through its landing, and few outsiders see more than the totem-post.

name: Xuvagol
held_by: The Root-Folk of Helstrom, a hunting clan
summary: Xuvagol is a Root-Folk hunting station on a forested rise at the western end of the jungle, a day beyond Tselan. Six people hunt the jungle edge from it and trade hides at Tselan.

name: Neexa-Lul
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Neexa-Lul is a small outpost on an islet in the lake's eastern reaches, between Marzai and Truowa, kept for a lake watch and egg-tending. Boats crossing between Marzai and Truowa often use its landing to wait out the wind.

name: Ranvos Landing
held_by: A ferry-keeper's family by the Vicecanons' leave
summary: A ferry stage and wayhouse on the eastern branch of the river south-east of Stormhold, on the road toward Helstrom.

name: Orji-Hael
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Orji-Hael is a small outpost south of Korydon on firm ground by the great southern water. It serves as a waystation. Boats going south toward Blackrose pause at its landing before they leave the sheltered water.

name: Tazhul
held_by: Root-Folk of Helstrom, an egg-tending station
summary: Tazhul is a small Root-Folk station in the marsh west of Inoja, a hunting and egg-tending post of Helstrom's people far from their Hist.

name: Thornway Watch
held_by: The Archwardens' garrison, from Fort Thornmoth
summary: Thornway Watch is a small toll post on the track from Tsonac to Thorn, a day's walk from Fort Thornmoth. A few of the fort's garrison keep it and take a toll from the stone and timber carts.

name: Yuvexa
held_by: The Root-Folk of Helstrom
summary: Yuvexa is a Root-Folk hunters' post on the south lip of the mesa, looking over the Balormaak and Vorannuhl ruins. Its families hunt, and guide the few who want to go to the ruins.

name: Redclay Watch
held_by: Aroxhu confederacy spear-watch
summary: Redclay Watch is a mound-top spear-post on the road between Renhu and Seafalls. The confederacy keeps it to take tolls from outside goods and stop coast robbers.

name: Marshgate Watch
held_by: Archwardens, detachment from Fort Thornmoth
summary: Marshgate Watch is a road post on the coast road south of Thorn. Wardens check goods and travellers moving between Thorn, the bight villages and Arorha.

name: Nuxhal
held_by: The Root-Folk of Helstrom
summary: Nuxhal is a Root-Folk hunters' post on the western mesa, where two families hunt and look out toward the smoke of Tenmal Pits. Its hides and reeds go to Tenmal and the pit crews.

name: Hokal-Ush
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Hokal-Ush is a small outpost on a hummock beside a river bend east of Helstrom, kept for hunting and fellrunner-feather trading. It trades feathers to the river-boats that come east from Helstrom and has little other dealing with outsiders.

name: Reeka-Veesa
held_by: The Sedge-Wardens of Jal-Veesa
summary: Reeka-Veesa is a Sedge-Warden post on the mesa's far west, on the road from Tenmal to Ranvos Landing. A few families cut reed, take feathers and keep their children away from Sahlpesh Cave.

name: Uzu-Tegh
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Uzu-Tegh is a small outpost on a low islet in the lake's northern shallows, kept for eel-trapping and a lake watch. Its eel-traps are known to every lake boatman, though few ever land on the islet.

name: Causeway-Head Post
held_by: A Vicecanon's reeve and two guards
summary: A road post on the northern trunk where it leaves Stormhold's causeway north-west of Fort Willowmoth, taking a small toll on reed and fish cargoes.

name: Banu-Veeth Post
held_by: Mine-Burner tribes of the Banujha
summary: Banu-Veeth Post is a small watch post in the Banujha Basin. It stands on the water at the south of the basin, covering the channel toward Soulrest.

name: Reed-Sill Weir
held_by: Veesa-Teeleel weir-wardens
summary: A weir-wardens' camp on the creek north-east of Gandranen, keeping the traps for Jal-Veesa.

name: Ashgate Post
held_by: A Vicecanon's reeve and two guards
summary: A stone road post west of Loriasel on the Slough Point road, watching the track toward the ruins.

name: Tzel-Haar
held_by: Hutan-Tzel naheesh
summary: Tzel-Haar is a small outpost on the Panther River's west bank, north-west of Helstrom, kept for a river watch and trade. It is a stopping point on the water routes through the Panther River country, known to few outsiders.

name: Jal-Resh Post
held_by: Mine-Burner tribes of the Banujha
summary: Jal-Resh Post is a small watch post in the Banujha Basin. It stands on the Banujha waters between Jarecai and Kharaxos.

name: Ukeel Station
held_by: Naka-Desh river-folk
summary: Ukeel Station is a small river station in the Banujha Basin. It stands on the banks of the Banujha, where Naka-Desh fishers net osheeja gar and trade at the water's edge.

name: Xal-Tarek
held_by: Banujha mine-burner watchers
summary: Xal-Tarek is a mine-burner watch post on the south coast of the cape, in the water, set to watch Soulrest's approaches.

name: Hutan-Aru
held_by: The Hutan-Tzel under an elder styled naheesh
summary: A fortified outpost of the Hutan-Tzel on a river branch in the far west, one of a chain along the river.

name: Vel-Sapha Stand
held_by: Root-Folk sap-gatherers from the interior
summary: A sap-tapping and egg-tending station of the Root-Folk, a long way west of Helstrom, at the edge of Barsaebica.

name: Xul-Banu Post
held_by: Mine-Burner tribes of the Banujha
summary: Xul-Banu Post is a small watch post in the Banujha Basin. It stands at the basin's north-west edge, facing Nha Enasa and Gul-Tej.

name: Olaxa Station
held_by: Root-Folk of Helstrom
summary: Olaxa Station is a small Root-Folk hunting and egg-tending station in the Banujha Basin. It lies in the basin's northern reeds, a stilt post with a drying rack and an egg-hut.

name: Sakeepa Station
held_by: Naka-Desh river-folk
summary: Sakeepa Station is a small river station in the Nha Enasa. It stands on the Nha Enasa channel east of Gideon, where the river-folk trade with Gul-Tej.

name: Deshaa Post
held_by: Mine-Burner tribes of the Banujha
summary: Deshaa Post is a small watch post in the Banujha Basin. It stands at the south-west basin edge, covering the road toward Soulrest and Chasepoint.

name: Ixu-Maan
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Ixu-Maan is a small outpost on a small rise south of Helstrom, between the river arms, kept for egg-tending and a night watch. The lamp on its rise is the last light on the city's south approach. Travellers take it as a sign to slow.

name: Nahk-Zeel Station
held_by: Naka-Desh river-folk
summary: Nahk-Zeel Station is a small river station in the Nha Enasa. It stands at the northern edge of Nha Enasa, close to Gul-Tej and the Paatru camps.

name: Hutan-Veel
held_by: The Hutan-Tzel under an elder styled naheesh
summary: A second Hutan-Tzel palisade outpost, far west, on the edge of the Cyrodiil border.

name: Reek-Anu
held_by: Naka-Desh river-folk
summary: Reek-Anu is a Naka-Desh river station at the northwest edge of the cape, a small riverbank hut group keeping fish gars and watching the water.

name: Sarth-Hul Station
held_by: Root-Folk of Helstrom
summary: Sarth-Hul Station is a small Root-Folk hunting and egg-tending station in the Nha Enasa. It lies deep in Nha Enasa's reeds, a stilt post where hunters tend a Hist sapling and a clutch of eggs.

name: Teth-Kasa Station
held_by: Naka-Desh river-folk
summary: Teth-Kasa Station is a small river station in the Kotherra Mangroves. It stands among the mangrove channels south of Gideon and is the Naka-Desh's western-most post.

name: Sedge-Kal Camp
held_by: Veesa-Teeleel reed-cutters on rotation
summary: A seasonal cutters' camp on the northern road beyond Jal-Veesa, where the reed is cut for Stormhold's mat-makers.

name: Vesh-Aneel
held_by: Root-Folk tree-minder of the nearest village tree
summary: Vesh-Aneel is a small outpost on an isolated hummock in the marsh south-west of Helstrom, kept for a hunters' camp and a waypoint on the long route to Nacydes. Hunters crossing to Nacydes rest here. It is the only dry ground for miles around.

name: Teel-Fen Weir
held_by: Veesa-Teeleel weir-wardens
summary: A weir-wardens' camp on the creek north-east of Gandranen, keeping traps for Jal-Veesa.

name: Hutan-Ketu
held_by: Hutan-Tzel naheesh
summary: Hutan-Ketu is a small outpost on the river west of Helstrom, at the Murkwood edge, kept for a go-between post between Helstrom and the west. It is a stopping point on the water routes through the Panther River country, known to few outsiders.

name: Zul-Meeka Station
held_by: Root-Folk of Helstrom
summary: Zul-Meeka Station is a small Root-Folk hunting and egg-tending station in the Banujha Basin. It lies on the south-east basin's edge, near the Lilmothiit den and the abandoned village.

name: Ovezza
held_by: Nothing living; the dead and river creatures
summary: Ovezza is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi town on the south shore of the bay, west of Guxal. The Knahaten Flu emptied it and the jungle has grown into it.

name: Oxayo
held_by: The Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac
summary: Oxayo is a hamlet of stone and timber above a river at the mesa's north-west, between Tselan and the Sarpa lands. It is a quarry hamlet and a lookout on the Sarpa road.

name: The Grey Tooth
held_by: No one; sea-birds
summary: The Grey Tooth is the one crag on Skeith Isle, a grey-green stone spire that seamen use as a mark. The summit gives a view of the whole coast.

name: Nacydes Watch
held_by: Chime-Keeper lookout parties
summary: Nacydes Watch is a ridge peak on the west of Aunike Ridge, above Nacydes, overlooking Paatru and Naga ground.

name: Aunike Crown
held_by: Chime-Keeper lookout parties
summary: Aunike Crown is the high point of the Aunike Ridge, above Tydeos, from which the marsh can be seen for hours.

name: Percar Scar
held_by: Nobody
summary: Percar Scar is a long strip of dead, fire-glassed ground on the Percar hills, left by the Great Burn. Gas vents and black snags mark it.

name: Stonecut Quarry
held_by: A quarry crew of Soulrest-quarter kin
summary: A working quarry on the Percar road, worked by a Soulrest-quarter crew for the harbour.

name: Redbank Quarry
held_by: A quarry crew of Soulrest-quarter kin
summary: A red-stone quarry on the south side of the cape.

name: Rainbreaker Keep
held_by: Marque Landing pirates, the Rainbreaker crew
summary: Rainbreaker Keep is an old Imperial sea-watch keep on Skeith Isle, left empty at the secession. The pirates of Marque Landing now use it as their strong room, and its undercroft holds their prisoners.

name: Renhu
held_by: Renhu elders, under the Aroxhu council
summary: Renhu is a coastal clay-mound village on an inlet east of Xibcan. Its people farm the mounds, net fish in the estuary and lodge travellers on the Seafalls road.

name: Sal-Axan
held_by: A village moot of Lilmoth-coast families, in the fort's shadow
summary: Sal-Axan is a village on the north coast of the northern Althii island, a short walk from Fort Reedmoth. It sells fish, rice and shell to the fort and houses its toll-keepers.

name: Salaxul
held_by: Soulrest merchant council reeve
summary: Salaxul is a south-coast village below Mir-Xal, a landing for coastal boats and a salt and shellfish station. It is the south stage of the Soulrest-Mir-Xal road.

name: Seafalls
held_by: The Spray-Folk of Seafalls, under their pilot-elder
summary: Seafalls is a cliff-and-surf village on the coast north of Archon, where a river drops to the sea. Its people pilot ships, keep a portage round the falls and live apart from the Hist.

name: Seafalls Lighthouse
held_by: The Spray-Folk of Seafalls, a keeper family
summary: Seafalls Lighthouse is the beacon on the point east of the village. A keeper family lights it each night to guide ships past the shoals.

name: Shalaia
held_by: A Three Waters raft-master family under the elder of Uluo
summary: Shalaia is a shellfish hamlet on the western edge of the bayou, in sight of Truowa's waters and Fort Gysilla's smoke. The Three Waters people here fish, and mostly keep away from the fort.

name: Wreck of the Salt Heron
held_by: Nobody; Natai salvagers work the wreck
summary: The Salt Heron is a Khajiit coaster out of Senchal, wrecked off Natai in shallow water. Natai's salvagers work her cargo.

name: The Kelp Lantern
held_by: Left to kelp and a slaughterfish shoal
summary: The Kelp Lantern is a brass diving sphere on the sea floor near Echo Deep, lost from an East Empire Company barge before the secession. Kelp has grown over it and its viewing glass still glows.

name: Wreck of the Tidewarden
held_by: No one; gulls, crabs and beachcombers
summary: The Tidewarden is a Khajiit-crewed merchant cog that ran aground on the shore north of Archon in the years Leyawiin was held and the Blackwood Road shut, and was never refloated. It is a beachcombers' site with a few valuables left and a ghost story.

name: Wreck of the Silt Bride
held_by: No one; the drowned dead of the hold
summary: Wreck of the Silt Bride is a Dunmer slaver brig lost off the coast of Thorn in the late Third Era, before the Red Year. Shackles still hang in her hold and the drowned crew and captives still walk it.

name: Wreck of the Pale Harvest
held_by: No one; sea creatures and the drowned crew
summary: The Pale Harvest was an East Empire Company saltrice freighter that went down in Hatandros Bight. Its cargo of rotted sacks and a ship's strongbox are still aboard.

name: Wreck of the Brindle Gull
held_by: No one; the drowned dead of the sloop
summary: Wreck of the Brindle Gull is a smuggler's sloop that went down on the Kornakim shoals running from a rival crew, with her strongbox still locked in the deckhouse.

name: Wreck of the Stormwidow
held_by: No one; scavengers from both camps
summary: The Stormwidow is a privateer galleon run onto the south-west beach of Skeith Isle. Both camps strip her, and her captain's strongbox is still unfound.

name: Wreck of the Resolute Crest
held_by: No one; the drowned marines
summary: Wreck of the Resolute Crest is a Septim man-of-war of Uriel V's Akavir fleet, sunk in deep water off Skeith Isle with its ballistae and an Akaviri chest still aboard.

name: Wreck of the Brine Gull
held_by: Nobody; Soulrest salvagers work the wreck
summary: The Brine Gull is a Valenwood coaster sunk off the south-west of the cape, on the sea floor near Acra-Tiin's islands.

name: The Grey Heron
held_by: No one: salvagers visit it
summary: The Grey Heron is the wreck of a Leyawiin merchantman that struck the bar off Gideon's estuary in the last years before the secession. It lies on the floor of Topal Bay with part of its Cyrodiilic cargo still in the hold.

name: The Sallow Anne
held_by: No one: salvagers visit it
summary: The Sallow Anne is a smuggler's sloop wrecked on the rocks off Aphon Isle while a rival crew chased it. Its moon sugar and Valenwood silk lie in the hold, and its captain's strongbox has never been found.

name: Siluo
held_by: A Three Waters raft-master family under the elder of Uluo
summary: Siluo is a reed-gatherers' hamlet on a hummock in the bayou west of the road. It supplies thatch and mat-reed to Uluo and keeps a trap-line of eels and crabs.

name: Slough Point
held_by: A council of Lukiul and Nibenese-descended families; Fort Rustmoth's garrison keeps the toll
summary: A frontier village at the old border crossing, built round the Imperial census-and-excise post beside a black river whose white bridge has lost its middle span. It lives on the Blackwood Road trade and the toll fort beside it.

name: Soulrest
held_by: A merchant council, the ex-Imperial civil office and river interests, in an unresolved contest; the Banujha tribes hold the hatching grounds
summary: Soulrest is Black Marsh's Third Era capital and its only city on the Topal Bay and Southern Sea corner, a port with no empire left to serve. Its government quarter is half empty, the mixed population lives off sea trade, salvage and the hidden Bramman's river and three groups contest who rules.

name: Southwatch Keep
held_by: A small garrison of the Archwardens, the An-Xileel successor administration, drawn from old Archein families
summary: Southwatch Keep is a stone fort at the south-western tip of the southern Althii island, facing the sea road to Lilmoth. A small Archwarden garrison lights its beacon and checks ships.

name: Stormhold
held_by: The Vicecanons of Stormhold (the office the city invented); the Hist tree in the town square
summary: The province's northern gate and one of its eight great cities: a stone-and-mud city on mounds and ravines beside the river that marks the Morrowind border, built over the Ayleid ruin of Silyanorn around a waterfall. In 4E 201 it is run by Vicecanons and holds the state's customs, its frontier offices and the province's largest and oldest Dunmer minority.

name: Teku-Sul Spire
held_by: Reef fish and a giant mudcrab
summary: Teku-Sul Spire is a drowned xanmeer tower on the sea floor of Benthic Yobesh. It lies closest to Lilmoth's drowned quarter and is half stripped.

name: Haxtil-Meht Spire
held_by: A slaughterfish school and the old fish that leads it
summary: Haxtil-Meht Spire is a drowned xanmeer tower on the sea floor of Benthic Yobesh. It stands near Echo Deep, half cleared, with slaughterfish in its flooded hall.

name: Zeshul-Tha Spire
held_by: A dreugh and its brood
summary: Zeshul-Tha Spire is a drowned xanmeer tower on the sea floor of Benthic Yobesh. It stands near Echo Deep and holds a dreugh's nest and hoard.

name: Naxiil-Ru Spire
held_by: Dreugh scouts
summary: Naxiil-Ru Spire is a drowned xanmeer tower on the sea floor of Benthic Yobesh. It stands north of Bell Station and dreugh scouts hold it.

name: Okhu-Thteel Spire
held_by: Slaughterfish, and the dead salvager's lamp
summary: Okhu-Thteel Spire is a lone drowned xanmeer tower on a sand plain, the furthest north-east of the spires, with a Hist-sap shrine on its summit.

name: Va-Seeth Spire
held_by: The grave of a failed salvage crew, and slaughterfish
summary: Va-Seeth Spire is a drowned xanmeer tower beside Bell Station's anchor chains, where a failed salvage crew lies in the lower gallery.

name: Thul-Kesh Spire
held_by: A drowned sea-priest's ghost
summary: Thul-Kesh Spire is the outermost drowned xanmeer tower, tall and pale on the edge of the deep, kept sealed by a sea-priest's ghost.

name: Surkina
held_by: A council of farm-holders by the Vicecanons' leave
summary: A village of raised stone farmsteads on the causeway road south of Stormhold, living on saltrice and market vegetables for the city.

name: Tapauo
held_by: A Three Waters raft-master family under the elder of Uluo
summary: Tapauo is a ricefield hamlet on the bayou channels north of Uluo, where the Three Waters people grow saltrice on floating beds. It is the tribe's granary.

name: Tarak Shan
held_by: Nobody; scavengers and wildlife
summary: Tarak Shan is a ruined Argonian stronghold on the water east of the washes, stormed by the Third Legion in the late Second Era.

name: Tei-Kur
held_by: A reed-lord council of the delta villages
summary: Tei-Kur is a delta village north-east of Blackrose in the farm country between the lake and the Lilmoth coast. It feeds the cities with its rice and sends its own to Delta Ferry.

name: Tenmal
held_by: A council of farm-holders by the Vicecanons' leave
summary: A village on the river road east of Stormhold, near the old Tenmar Wall junction, living on river trade and the mine at its back.

name: Thorn
held_by: Vicecanons and the saltrice field-owners
summary: Thorn is the north-east's one large city, a grassland border town on the Padomaic coast beside the road to Tear in Morrowind. It lives on saltrice, tolls and smuggling and is run by Vicecanons and the families who hold the old saltrice fields. Its guards are paid to look the other way.

name: Toklea
held_by: A council of craft-masters; no Archwarden garrison
summary: Toklea is a Kothringi-named town on a stone footing where the river forks, resettled by Argonians after 2E 560. It is a tidy, chime-hung trading town on the road between Blackrose and Helstrom.

name: Hanaxi Roost
held_by: A Sarpa warband
summary: Hanaxi Roost is a camp of the winged Sarpa on the western mesa edge, facing Middle Argonia. The Sarpa kill strangers on sight.

name: Seth-Alaxh Roost
held_by: The Sarpa of the Seth-Alaxh roost
summary: Seth-Alaxh Roost is a winged Sarpa camp in the marsh between Aroxhu and Yulca. They are hostile to strangers and fire down on them from high perches.

name: Zeeraxun Roost
held_by: The Sarpa of the Zeeraxun roost
summary: Zeeraxun Roost is a camp of the winged Sarpa on a rise in the marsh behind Hatandros Bight. They keep apart, drive off outsiders and stay near the Virtluush ruin.

name: Tumnatu Cattail Camp
held_by: The Tumnatu hunters
summary: Tumnatu Cattail Camp is a Tumnatu camp in the Ultherus swamp near Korydon.

name: Tumnatu Reed Camp
held_by: The Tumnatu hunters
summary: Tumnatu Reed Camp is a Tumnatu camp on the lake's north shore.

name: Hiss-Bank Camp
held_by: A tribeless Naga band
summary: Hiss-Bank Camp is a Naga camp on the western river bank.

name: Mud-Croak Camp
held_by: A band of Paatru
summary: Mud-Croak Camp is a Paatru camp west of Murkwood.

name: Ixha-Neeth Camp
held_by: A Paatru hunting party of the Middle Argonian forest
summary: Ixha-Neeth Camp is a Paatru hunters' camp in the Nha Enasa. It lies on a riverbank among reeds, with a smoke-rack and a drawn-up boat.

name: Veshu-Taal Camp
held_by: A Paatru hunting party of the Middle Argonian forest
summary: Veshu-Taal Camp is a Paatru hunters' camp in the Banujha Basin. It lies on dry ground at the basin's north edge, close to Mine-Burner land.

name: Karsh-Naal Camp
held_by: A band of tribeless Naga
summary: A Naga camp in the marsh south of Stormhold, where the brigands of the road-sides live between raids.

name: Dry-Fang Camp
held_by: A tribeless Naga band
summary: Dry-Fang Camp is a Naga camp on dry ground north of Helstrom.

name: Nul-Sakeesh Camp
held_by: A Paatru hunting party of the Middle Argonian forest
summary: Nul-Sakeesh Camp is a Paatru hunters' camp in the Nha Enasa. It lies against a Kothringi ruin, whose standing walls the hunters roof for shelter.

name: Salt-Tooth Camp
held_by: A tribeless Naga band
summary: Salt-Tooth Camp is a Naga camp in the marsh south-west of Helstrom.

name: Ushaan Camp
held_by: A band of tribeless Naga
summary: A Naga camp in the marsh south of Gandranen, living off the road traffic.

name: Truowa
held_by: A merchant council allied to Lilmoth's
summary: Truowa is a small trading city on the south-east shore of Lake Ulaish, where the lake's waters meet the Nushara channels toward Lilmoth. A merchant council tied to Lilmoth's commerce runs it. It is the interior's lake harbour, richer than the villages around it and wary of the Archwardens.

name: Tselan
held_by: The Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac
summary: Tselan is a hamlet of stone and timber on the river west of Tsonac, one of the Stone-Sleepers' outlying hamlets. It supplies Tsonac with quarried stone and river fish.

name: Tsonac
held_by: The Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac, ruled by a council of elders and a tree-minder
summary: Tsonac is a terraced city of stone and timber at the head of the bay's inlet, built around a Hist its people say is asleep. It is the capital of the Arnesian jungle, sells stone and timber to Thorn and owes the Archwardens nothing but courtesy.

name: Tydeos
held_by: A family of Chime-Keepers
summary: Tydeos is a hamlet on firm ground at the foot of the Aunike Ridge's southern peak. The families keep chimes, lizard-pens and a path across the ridge to the western waters.

name: Uluo
held_by: The elder of the Three Waters Tribe and the tribe's council of raft-masters
summary: Uluo is the one town of the Three Waters Tribe, on the north shore of the Althii islands facing the Nushara Bayou. It is the seat of the tribe's elder and the market where the bayou hamlets sell rice, shellfish and reed. The tribe deals with Archon as an equal and with Lilmoth by the back-water routes.

name: Umpholo
held_by: A small river village of Lukiul and Naka-Desh families; nobody rules it
summary: A river village at the empty stone chapel of the Maran mission, in the far west. Its people live around a church that the swamp overgrew two centuries ago.

name: Vorannuhl
held_by: Nothing living; the flu-dead and what they guard
summary: Vorannuhl is a remote Cantemiric Velothi ruin deep on the mesa near the Middle Argonian edge. Its dead lie undisturbed and its halls are the deepest of the east.

name: Ruined Velothi Shrine of Nyrath-Ven
held_by: The dead; Velothi ghosts the Flu left behind; Archon's Dunmer families tend one niche, and the harbour folk and the Aroxhu otherwise avoid it
summary: A stepped-dome shrine of the Cantemiric Velothi, Dunmer settlers killed by the Knahaten Flu by 2E 603, on dry ground near Archon. It is a ruin with undead and old grave-goods that the Aroxhu and most of Archon avoid.

name: Anvadas
held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
summary: Anvadas is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding on a mud-ridge in the marsh south of Gaweja, held by ghosts, skeletal guards and crocodiles.

name: Sethiral
held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
summary: Sethiral is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding at Yina, on the river bank above the hamlet. Its lower halls are shut and held by the household's ghosts.

name: Mazurath
held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
summary: Mazurath is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi holding on the headland south of Khiar. A spell-fire burns on its upper tier and ghosts and smugglers hold the halls.

name: Vicrium
held_by: Seafalls families and Aroxhu clay-miners, jointly
summary: Vicrium is an old ochre and alum mine in the clay country behind Seafalls. The Imperial name has stayed in use. Its lower galleries run deeper than the miners work.

name: Virtluush
held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts and Sarpa scouts
summary: Virtluush is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi settlement inland of Hatandros Bight, once a river-fort. A Sarpa roost sits beside it.

name: Xi-Inou
held_by: A Three Waters raft-master family under the elder of Uluo
summary: Xi-Inou is a Three Waters hamlet on the west bank of Archon's estuary, where bayou rafts hand their loads to harbour boats. It is the bayou's nearest door to the sea.

name: Xibcan
held_by: The Agaceph of Xibcan
summary: Xibcan is an Agaceph hamlet on a marsh island. Its people keep a small shelf of books taken from a dead Maran outstation and sell some to strangers.

name: Yalugo
held_by: Two farm families of the Stormhold manner
summary: Yalugo is a hamlet on the south shore of Lake Ulaish, on the boat road between Truowa and the Korydon waters. Its stone-footed farms supply rice and fish to Fort Gysilla's garrison and to passing traders.

name: Yina
held_by: The Agaceph of Yina
summary: Yina is an Agaceph hamlet built round the foot of the Sethiral ruin. Its people live in the lee of the old stones, which they use as a lookout and a fort.

name: Ysan
held_by: Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac, a landing held for Tsonac
summary: Ysan is a small coastal landing of Tsonac's stone-building people on Hatandros Bight. Quarried stone and timber come down here by river to be shipped to Thorn.

name: Yulca
held_by: The Agaceph of Yulca, a council of readers
summary: Yulca is the Agaceph's one town, on the great lake in Okuwun-Rahei's west. It is a town of illusionists and rafters who keep books taken from dead Maran missions.

name: Yuva-Goli
held_by: Root-Folk of Helstrom, tide-station
summary: Yuva-Goli is a Root-Folk station on the outer coast of Hatandros Bight, the Hist forest's watch on the Padomaic. Its few people gather shore-wrack and sea-salt and keep a lookout.
